scores.evidence: Phase 1: "Event logging to Kafka and the lakehouse, label pipeline, rules engine on the auth path, latency harness"
scores.rationale: Phases broadly go data → features → model → rollout, but the architecture and feature design are specified up front and the ordering is loosely justified; the control group comes last though it affects labels.

scores.evidence: Phase 1 ... "rules engine on the auth path, latency harness"
scores.rationale: Phase 1 puts a rules engine on the auth path, which is somewhat end-to-end, but it is a 6-week bundle, not a thin slice through to production decisions, and no model or step-up is included.

scores.evidence: "Fall back to rules only, then approve with limits (fail-open with limits)"
scores.rationale: A defaults table exists, but it has no flip conditions or revisit triggers, and irreversible choices such as the feature store, the Kafka/Flink stack, and the tokenization point are not listed as gates.
Nothing orders work within phases by blast radius; items are just listed.

scores.evidence: "Tokenize the full card number (PAN) at the edge so the fraud stack sees only tokens."
scores.rationale: Security has a standalone section, but the phased delivery table never mentions it, so it is not threaded through the phases.

scores.evidence: Phase 2: "first GBDT model in shadow mode, monitoring dashboards"
scores.rationale: Monitoring is detailed in section 6, but the phases introduce dashboards only in Phase 2, with just a latency harness in Phase 1.

scores.evidence: "log the exact feature vector served with every decision... point-in-time joins"
scores.rationale: Train/serve skew and versioned rules and models are covered, but there is no reproducible build, environment, or infrastructure treatment per phase.

scores.evidence: "a hard timeout on the scorer, then rules only, then default approve under a capped amount."
scores.rationale: Fallbacks and kill switches are concrete, but they sit in a standalone section and are not placed in each phase.

scores.evidence: "Kill switches: per model, per rule, and per segment"; "shadow mode (score everything, act on nothing"
scores.rationale: The system is a GBDT fraud model (classical ML) with human analysts, rules, kill switches, and shadow/canary rollout. It has no explicit layered AI ordering of defenses, budgets, and human-in-the-loop before capabilities, and the feedback loop lands in Phase 3.

scores.evidence: "Phase 4 | 18+ | Device and graph features, anomaly model, automated retraining, control group"
scores.rationale: Later work is listed in Phase 4 and as optional add-ons, but there are no pull-forward conditions.

note: A solid domain-level fraud design with good technical depth, but it is weak on process structure: no flip conditions, no blast-radius ordering, and security, observability, and resilience are not threaded through the phases.
